title: Conversation
coreMove: Listen for knowledge display inside talk that claims to be only information exchange.
sourcePressure: The source argues that conversation is not only information exchange; it also displays the ability to know and learn, including in news and academic research.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The writer turns conversation into communication tips and misses status display around knowing and learning.

sourceAnchors.name: conversation as more than information exchange
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says people talk not just to exchange information.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The fact being shared is often only half the transaction.

sourceAnchors.name: showing off ability to know and learn
sourceAnchors.detail: The source says conversation can display the ability to know and learn.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: A person can be offering news and auditioning as the kind of mind worth having nearby.

sourceAnchors.name: news and academic research as display arenas
sourceAnchors.detail: The source connects the theory to news and academic research as social arenas where knowledge display matters.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The headline and the seminar question both let people show what kind of knower they are.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person You direct address, retrospective It took her three weeks to see, question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.audience: a coordinator keeping useful updates from becoming expertise contests
exampleSpecs.stakes: flood information must move without turning every speaker into a status act
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Laura splits the briefing into facts, needs, and offers after Etienne uses river-level jargon to display expertise instead of move sandbags.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The river map curls at the corners under a strip of blue tape.
mustAvoid: disaster example from ch2 repeated as coalition only

exampleSpecs.domain: book club argument over an essay
exampleSpecs.audience: a host noticing members compete to have read the smarter source
exampleSpecs.stakes: the group may value display over shared understanding
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: "That was in the New Yorker piece," Devon says, and Kasia asks what decision the reference changes for their local project.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "That was in the New Yorker piece," Devon says before anyone mentions the essay.

exampleSpecs.audience: an incident commander separating useful learning from clever commentary
exampleSpecs.stakes: performative expertise slows repair during outage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pablo pins a three-field update template after Maja posts the clever root-cause theory before checking the logs.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: The alert tone repeats under a wall of speculative messages.

exampleSpecs.audience: a judge distinguishing a child's learning from parent display
exampleSpecs.stakes: knowledge performance can crowd out actual learning
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You ask the student to explain the failed trial, not the polished poster, and watch whether the learning belongs to the child or the parent.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You see the glitter title before you see the crossed-out trial notes.

exampleSpecs.audience: a visiting scholar hearing questions as status bids
exampleSpecs.stakes: research discussion can become a display arena
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Which question changes the paper, and which one only tells the room who read the footnotes?
exampleSpecs.firstImage: Which question leaves the paper different after it lands?

exampleSpecs.domain: morning news rundown at a logistics firm
exampleSpecs.audience: a supervisor keeping news talk from becoming tribal display
exampleSpecs.stakes: the shift needs weather and port facts, not prestige through commentary
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: It took Laura one delayed truck to realize the most informed-sounding rundown had skipped the port closure that mattered.
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Laura one delayed truck to distrust the cleverest recap.

skillTargets: detect knowledge display in information-sharing settings
separate useful talk from status talk
apply the know-and-learn signal to news and research contexts

tryThisNowSpec: In one conversation today, mark each contribution as useful information, ability display, alliance signal, or some mix of the three.
